in_text_mentions: erred to our Pediatric Endocrinology Department for short stature. At first evaluation she was 1.6 years old. She presented a symmetrical short stature: height was 72.5 cm (−2.58 SDS), sitting height was 46.1 cm (−2.3 SDS), sitting height/height ratio was 0.63 (0 SDS), weight was 8.2 kg (−3.15 SDS) and head circumference was 46.8 cm (+0.31 SDS). She was prepuberal. Facial features included frontal bossing and depressed nasal bridge. No other congenital abnormalities were evident (Fig. 1). Subscapular skinfold was 18.4 mm, tricipital skinfold 12.5 mm.Fig. 1Physical presentation at 3.8 years old

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Full-body clinical photograph of the reported 28-year-old woman with suspected Laron syndrome; the caption explicitly states severe proportional short stature, a hallmark manifestation of Laron syndrome, and the image visibly confirms marked short stature. B: Lateral facial profile of the same Laron syndrome patient; the caption and in-text describe frontal bossing and a saddle-shaped/depressed nasal ridge with an underdeveloped mandible, which are characteristic craniofacial features of Laron syndrome. C: Close-up ocular photograph of the same patient showing a distinct blue-tinted sclera, as stated in the caption and in-text for this Laron syndrome case. The finding is clearly present but is not represented in the allowed vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding; it is an uncommon ocular sign in Laron syndrome.

Inspection of the eyes revealed blue-tinted sclera (Fig. 1). Peripheral lean muscle wasting was observed. Limb examination revealed deformities and abnormal curvatures, especially in the distal leg and distal humerus. Pubertal development was appropriate, with menarche at 13 years, Tanner stage IV sexual maturation, and regular menstrual function. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Real patient plain radiograph from a Laron syndrome case report whose title specifies severe low bone density for age; the caption states this panel shows severe generalized osteopenia with multiple healed fractures. No allowed vocabulary key matches these skeletal findings, so they are recorded as proposed findings. B: Real patient radiograph in the same Laron syndrome case; caption specifically describes an active complete fracture at the distal one-third of the humeral shaft, consistent with the article title's severe low bone-density presentation. The fracture finding is not in the allowed vocabulary and is therefore proposed only. C: Real patient knee radiographs from the Laron syndrome case report; caption groups panel C with panel A as showing severe generalized osteopenia and multiple healed fractures. The disease-focused article title supports attribution, while the skeletal findings themselves are recorded as proposed findings.

in_text_mentions: Plain radiographs demonstrated severe osteopenia with multiple healed fractures. A complete fracture was present at the distal one-third of the shaft of the humerus (Fig. 2).
